messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Canary failure detected in eu-west1. Error rate >5% for route /v1/generate. Paging on-call (sara). See alert: https://alerts.redwood.example/INC-1729992

sara: i'm seeing the spike on the canary dashboard, started ~1729991940, looks like 502s and 415s. tagging josh +meera

josh: investigating traces now, pulling up gateway logs. :eyes:

meera: canary shows 3 instances of the new routing rule, all in eu-west1. traffic mix is ~10% to new variant. quick question — did we change headers in the gateway in the last deploy?

josh: yes — commit 9f8a7b0 normalized content-type to strip charset. new model variant `mosaic-large-q4` expects exact header `application/json; charset=utf-8` (legacy quirk). without charset it returns 415 and some internal adapters convert to 502. root cause looks like header mismatch + a couple large requests hitting kv cache path.

rahul: that's... awkward. that commit was meant to standardize things, not break downstream assumptions. we should kill the routing flag and fallback to old variant. can someone flip the flag?

meera: on it. flipping `FF_ROUTE_NEW_VARIANT` to `false` in LaunchDarkly now.

meera: done — flag off. admin change id: LD-4482. :white_check_mark: metrics update in 30s.

eng-sre-bot: Feature flag change propagated to 12 services in eu-west1 (3 clusters). Rolling pressure reduced.

josh: seeing immediate drop in 415s but a residual 502 tail persists from requests that hit the new variant earlier and hung. i'm going to prepare a single-commit hotfix to set a default charset when absent to avoid mismatch. patch will be revert-ish: keep normalization but default to `; charset=utf-8`.

sara: go ahead. keep it to a single commit and we can expedite deploy. scope: gateway header handling only.

josh: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/gateway/pulls/3219 — patch summary:
```
- if Content-Type missing charset, append `; charset=utf-8`
- preserve existing normalization otherwise
- add unit + lightweight e2e for mosaic-large-q4 handshake
```

rahul: ACK. i'll approve and merge once CI passes. we should also prepare a quick rollback plan in case deploy regresses.

josh: CI green, merging. Merge commit: 3b4c2f1. Deploy command: `./deploy promote --service gateway --image gateway:3b4c2f1 --stages canary,prod --timeout 15m`

eng-sre-bot: Deploy started: gateway:3b4c2f1 -> canary (eu-west1). Canary health: 0/3 -> 1/3 passing -> 3/3 passing.

josh: hotfix live on canary, telemetry shows 502s down to baseline, 415s gone. rolling to prod now.

meera: customer-impact quick note: approx 2.4% of RU for eu-west customers affected for ~18 minutes, no requests dropped permanently, a handful of automated retries triggered. CS notified top 5 impacted customers via status page update and email.

cs-notify-bot: Status update posted: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1729992 — message: "Intermittent 502/415 observed for eu-west customers during a canary rollout; mitigated by disabling new routing and hotfix. No data loss."

rahul: post-incident action items (short):
- add e2e that validates model-variant handshake header set (owner: josh)
- add canary guard that detects immediate header-mismatch spikes and auto-fallback (owner: meera)
- revert normalization-only change in favor of defaulting behavior in gateway (owner: infra)

sara: great work. keeping incident open until 30m stable window completes. thank you all for quick turn. :clap:

oncall-bot: Incident resolved at 1729992520 — Canary error rate back to baseline, feature flag remained off until hotfix rolled. Closing page. :tada:
